title: Supplements are (mostly) useless
summary: NH explains that he considers about 90% of supplements nonsense and takes only protein powder and creatine, for personal convenience and because he must limit red meat. He recounts experiments with fish oil, MSM and bee pollen, argues nutrition is overrated once mastered and that training matters most, and condemns the supplement-driven fitness industry.
claims: About 90% of supplements are nonsense that does not work, and some are dangerous
Supplements only provide what food can, in a more concentrated ratio; keeping that in mind lets you avoid most of them
Weight gainers and carb powders are stupid; make your own shake or just eat rice
He uses whey or pea protein for convenience: he needs few calories to maintain, avoids animal products for genetic health reasons, has a low appetite and eats one to two meals a day
Pick a protein powder that is actually protein, without lots of carbs or added sugar
Creatine works great for him: no hair loss (his hair is thicker than ever), longer and higher-volume workouts, and intramuscular water that makes him stronger and look bigger
He checks his bloodwork every six months to make sure creatine does no damage
Creatine replaces the red meat he has to minimize for health reasons
He tries cheap supplements not obviously marketed to beginners, and stops anything that shows no improvement
He took fish oil for a long time with no effect and stopped when his doctor said too much omega-3 was bad for him
He takes MSM powder once or twice a week for tendon health; it improved his knee tendinitis and he has used it for years
He uses bee pollen with his own careful protocol to treat his pollen allergy, warning that allergic people risk anaphylactic shock
Nutrition is overrated: once you eat clean whole foods and understand macros and micros, there is little left to gain; quitting milk made him much less puffy but it was a one-time change
The 70% nutrition, 20% training, 10% recovery idea is idiotic; training is at least 50% and becomes more important as you advance
He took no supplements at all for his first seven years and grew fine on food and water
No supplement will make you big; a flashy tub that does may contain illegal substances
The fitness industry has jacked people, some on PEDs, selling supplements because hard training cannot be sold
He sometimes takes B12 without noticing a difference, takes no pre-workout, drinks no coffee and refuses to depend on stimulants
For intra-workout energy a carb drink is enough, and plain water is perfectly fine
